Core: FileSystemTable needs to skip file cleanup after task failure under some boundary conditions.
We found that under some boundary conditions, HadoopCatalogTable will suffer from data file loss.
Since our Spark uses an LLAP-like runtime model(Long live and process),We have multiple sparkjobs running in the same spark-application, we need to take into account some additional runtime exceptions.
The problem is in BaseFileRewriteAction::doReplace.
When an exception is caught, if it is an unrecognised exception, Spark will clean up the data file for this commit.(only datafile,not have metafile)
But if we use HadoopCatalog, its commit method is not atomic for now.
HadoopCatalog's commit method needs to operate the file in hdfs several times, if in the process of operating the file, due to other DAG triggered RuntimeException, and it happens that Iceberg's metadata has been submitted, but the entire commit method is not finished. The call to the commit method will throw a RunTimeException. Caught by the doReplace method. Triggers a cleanup of the data file.
The end result is that the metafile is written, but the corresponding datafile is cleaned up.
I've changed the logic of commit so that when the versionhint is modified, if there is an exception at that point, we will skip the data cleanup session.
title: Core: FileSystemCatalogTable needs to skip file cleanup after task failure under some boundary conditions.

This is a maintenance release that fixes several minor defects and a regression in the Fluent module
causing the response body truncation discovered since release 5.3.
Change Log

Restored backwards-compatible #createSocket calls in

discarded instead of plain IllegalStateException.
Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski

HTTPCLIENT-2312: Fixed response body truncation in the fluent API (#521).
Contributed by Arturo Bernal

HTTPCLIENT-2313: Fixed NullPointerException in PoolingHttpClientConnectionManager when debug
logging is enabled.
Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski

Release 5.3
This is the first GA release in the 5.3 release series. This release finalizes the 5.3 APIs
and also includes all bug fixes from the 5.2 release branch.
The 5.3 release series introduces support for the Bearer authentication scheme (RFC 6750) and
deprecates NTLM and GSS-based experimental authentication schemes in favor of Basic / Bearer
authentication with TLS.

Introduction of the Bearer authentication scheme.

Deprecation of the NTLM authentication scheme.

Deprecation of the GSS-based experimental authentication schemes.
